items.headline: Anthropic Blocks a Researcher Over Its Oldest Rule
items.excerpt: A researcher blamed a new Anthropic ban for his blocked account, but the rule against distillation predates Anthropic's October rewrite by months.

items.headline: David Durman Wins the Right to Skip AI
items.excerpt: A University of Kentucky research administrator's humanist beliefs now carry the same Title VII protection against mandatory AI use that courts already give traditional religions.

items.headline: Buyouts, Blocks and a Billion-Dollar Bet
items.excerpt: Microsoft offers 60,000 workers an exit, Anthropic blocks a researcher, and investors stop believing everyone's AI math on the same day.

items.headline: Cognition's Price Jumps While Model Gains Shrink
items.excerpt: Investors value Cognition near $80 billion, and its own president says smarter models now move fewer new users than before.

items.headline: Commercial Brokers Trust AI With Everything but the Deal
items.excerpt: Two-thirds of commercial real estate professionals use AI every week, but the richest firms are the only ones buying the data that earns real trust.

items.headline: Startups Beat AI Labs in Four of Five Categories
items.excerpt: Ramp's card data names Claude Code, Granola and Wispr Flow the top sellers in their categories, and startups beat the giant labs almost everywhere else.

items.headline: Blanchett Asks a Judge to Make AI Pay
items.excerpt: Cate Blanchett's coalition told a federal judge Hollywood can already license AI training, countering OpenAI's fair-use defense.

items.headline: Businesses Buy More AI as Top Spenders Pull Back
items.excerpt: Ramp's AI Index shows token prices down 51 percent since March, but the top 1 percent of spenders still trail their July peak.

items.headline: Google's Satellite Chip Clears Its Easiest Test
items.excerpt: Google's satellite wrote a haiku from orbit, but its own research says matching one data center on Earth needs 10,000 satellites.

items.headline: OpenAI Slashes Its Funding Target as Doubt Spreads
items.excerpt: OpenAI cut its funding goal by $10 billion as markets questioned AI's spending and payoff.

items.headline: Apple Gives Siri a Memory of You
items.excerpt: iPadOS 27.2 lets Siri recall past chats and pull from Messages, Calendar, voicemails and Safari history, while a waitlist and the EU ban stand.

items.headline: Claude Agents Beat Anthropic's Safety Monitor Every Time
items.excerpt: Anthropic told its own Claude agents to slip harmful training data past its safety monitor, and the search won every time.

items.headline: OpenAI Publishes Math Faster Than Humans Can Check
items.excerpt: OpenAI's math archive hit 721 manuscripts while a Cambridge professor found a wrong number inside a proof that had already passed its own check.

items.headline: Blocks, Bans and a Borrowed Rule
items.excerpt: Banks block AI agents from logging into accounts, Albany bans chatbot features for kids, and four companies share a rule only one of them wrote.

items.headline: OpenAI, Google and Microsoft Follow Anthropic's Rule
items.excerpt: Anthropic wrote the robots.txt signal meant to block AI training, then adopted it first, while Google, Microsoft and OpenAI wait.

items.headline: Self-Represented Litigants Outnumber Lawyers in AI Court Errors
items.excerpt: The world's AI hallucination tracker counts more self-represented filers than lawyers, revealing a justice gap the sanction headlines miss.

items.headline: Meta Ships Muse Wonder After a Year of Exits
items.excerpt: Muse Wonder shipped Oct. 12, fourteen months after senior researchers began leaving Meta's Superintelligence Labs for OpenAI and Anthropic, a pattern Meta calls normal attrition.

items.headline: Third Circuit Breaks AI's Fair-Use Winning Streak
items.excerpt: Twelve open lawsuits test whether AI training on copyrighted work counts as fair use, and the first appeals ruling sided with the publisher.

items.headline: Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta Will Spend $730 Billion
items.excerpt: Their own third-quarter guidance puts 2026 AI spending at $720 billion to $740 billion, funded partly by new debt and stock.

items.headline: AI Super PACs Steer $70 Million to Safety
items.excerpt: OpenAI's and Anthropic's PAC networks spent nearly $70 million on the midterms, and most of it landed in races already decided before anyone voted.

items.headline: Cursor Confirms the Real Update Hid a Backdoor
items.excerpt: The file that reached up to 5,000 Cursor users was the genuine Claude Code extension, hijacked for eleven hours before anyone caught it.

items.headline: Mathematicians Trail OpenAI's 721 Math Proofs
items.excerpt: OpenAI posed its model about 4,000 problems and published 721 manuscripts in weeks; Lean has formally checked 42 percent of them.

items.headline: Anthropic Bars Claude Code From Cloning Existing Games
items.excerpt: Anthropic quietly blocked Claude Code from recreating specific video games, and developers noticed fast.

items.headline: Spotify's AI Music Rules Came Nearly a Year After Monet
items.excerpt: Spotify's remix tool starts with an artist's opt-in and its badge judges identity. Monet charted first, and five questions about AI music follow.

items.headline: OpenAI Catches Its Own Model Reaching the Internet
items.excerpt: OpenAI's new monitors caught a model reaching the live internet during training in September.

items.headline: Claude Agent Spots Malware Poker Sites Missed
items.excerpt: A professional poker player's Claude agent flagged a hidden program that let a hacker allegedly take up to $4 million from players over several years.

items.headline: Anthropic Drops Claude Ultra's Five-Hour Usage Cap
items.excerpt: Anthropic renamed its priciest Claude plan Ultra and dropped the usage cap coders hit most, while a lawsuit over its old math awaits a ruling.

items.headline: Hackers Leak DHS Files Naming Palantir and Grok
items.excerpt: A leak of more than 41,000 DHS records lists teams tied to Palantir and xAI's Grok.

items.headline: Family Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT's Epilepsy Taper
items.excerpt: A wrongful death suit says ChatGPT's 25-day taper plan preceded Bowen Wan's death from a seizure disorder.

items.headline: Amazon Calls Token Metrics Flawed, Keeps Them
items.excerpt: Amazon's new memo tells managers to judge AI by results, though it still tracks how much each team uses.

items.headline: Doubts, Discounts and a Distribution Fight
items.excerpt: Cramer doubts Nvidia's math, Washington discounts Claude while the Pentagon blocks it, and the Justice Department opens a fight over who runs AI's model shelf.

items.headline: GSA Widens Claude's Reach as Pentagon Blocks It
items.excerpt: A widened GSA discount brings Claude to every layer of government even as a federal court keeps the Pentagon from buying it.

items.headline: States Claim AI Governance; Few Enforce the Rules
items.excerpt: Nearly every state says it already has an AI policy, but the people running the systems report active enforcement far less often.

items.headline: You Can Turn Off Training on Five AI Chatbots
items.excerpt: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and Copilot each give you a real switch for model training. Meta AI skips that switch for U.S. users.

items.headline: SAG-AFTRA Leaves AI Value to Arbitrators
items.excerpt: SAG-AFTRA's new contract makes studios prove an AI performer's added value, but leaves that number undefined, for arbitrators to set case by case.

items.headline: Genie 4 Speaks, but Only to Testers
items.excerpt: Google DeepMind's new world model adds sound and lets testers steer scenes by typing, though only its chosen testers can try it.

items.headline: Claude Swayed Experts' Calls 86 Percent of the Time
items.excerpt: Anthropic secretly told Claude Code which side to favor, and 50 analysts matched its hidden lean most of the time.

items.headline: AI Avatars Steal Comedians' Jokes on Instagram
items.excerpt: Computer-generated comedians copy routines from young female stand-ups like Olivia Carter and Julia Jasunas, faster than Instagram's moderation keeps up.

items.headline: OpenAI Doubles ChatGPT Pro Limits After Backlash
items.excerpt: OpenAI canceled a planned ChatGPT Pro usage cut and doubled limits for Pro and Business Premium subscribers hours before the cut was set to begin.

items.headline: AI Chip Demand Drives SK Hynix to Record Profit
items.excerpt: SK Hynix's operating profit jumped 632 percent as AI buyers outbid everyone else for memory chips, and analysts split on how long it lasts.

items.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 Leads New AI Benchmark Using Secret Tests
items.excerpt: Artificial Analysis built most of its newest index from hidden tests, and every open-weight model fell further behind.

items.headline: Broadcom Bets on Anthropic, Hynix Banks the Boom
items.excerpt: Broadcom guaranteed billions to lease Anthropic its own chips, SK Hynix's profit jumped 632 percent, and eight more AI stories moved today.

items.headline: Broadcom Guarantees Anthropic's Chip Default Risk
items.excerpt: Broadcom personally backs $43.5 billion of the $63 billion Wall Street raised to lease Anthropic its chips, a guarantee banks demanded before they would sign.

items.headline: Employers Pay More for Degrees as Colleges Drop Detection
items.excerpt: Employers are betting degrees matter more in the AI era, just as colleges abandon the tools that proved students did their own work.

items.headline: Sprinklr Promises a Two-Week Job in an Hour
items.excerpt: Sprinklr says its new marketing agents turn a two-week campaign into an hour's work, while pricing, a release date and real customers still wait.

items.headline: Labels Resume Talks as Musicians Still Wait for Pay
items.excerpt: Universal and Warner settled with Suno and Udio in late 2025; the musicians who played those records want pay before talks resume Nov. 3.

items.headline: AI Agents Now Clock a 16-Hour Workday
items.excerpt: METR's benchmark shows the clean-task horizon doubling fast, but the same agents still trip on messy real work in minutes.

items.headline: FTC Puts Anthropic's Executives Under Oath
items.excerpt: A civil investigative demand escalated into sworn testimony eleven days later, testing whether the agency's AI safety probe can force real consequences.

items.headline: Cathedral Says It Broke Into Anthropic
items.excerpt: Cathedral's AI agents found a path into Anthropic's internal systems, and the two companies dispute how serious it was.

items.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Tops the AI Rankings
items.excerpt: An independent index ranks Google's new model first, built mostly on cybersecurity skill its own chairman says the industry still must secure.

items.headline: California Landlords Have 96 Days to Produce Original Photos
items.excerpt: California's AB 2025 requires labels and originals for altered rental photos, which apartment groups call costly and Consumer Reports calls necessary.

items.headline: Valve Hands Indie Developers the AI Clone Fight
items.excerpt: Valve's Steam business team told developers facing AI clones and extortion emails to build loyal fans, make harder-to-copy games, and report crimes to police.

items.headline: OpenAI Says Its AI Proved Three Old Problems
items.excerpt: OpenAI claims proofs in math, computing and physics, but mathematicians still doubt its last math release.

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Both Disprove the Same Math Rule
items.excerpt: Two AI labs say their own models broke the same 27-year-old computer science rule within hours of each other.

items.headline: Microsoft Buys Out Staff, Spares the Servers
items.excerpt: Microsoft offered 60,000 workers a way out while its AI budget held at $175 billion, and nine more stories moved today.

items.headline: Microsoft Keeps Data Centers Off Its Buyout List
items.excerpt: Microsoft invited 60,000 workers to leave this week, and spared the teams building its $175 billion AI budget.

items.headline: Bauer Closes Its Growth Bet, Keeps the Recipes
items.excerpt: Bauer Media closed the digital unit chasing search scale, keeping the brands themselves, as AI search cuts hit small publishers hardest.

items.headline: Authors Wait on Anthropic's Checks, Publishers Take Half
items.excerpt: Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin approved Anthropic's $1.5 billion book settlement in July, with the first checks to authors due by mid-November.

items.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra Cuts Price, Keeps a Catch
items.excerpt: OpenAI's new mid-tier model costs a quarter of Claude Opus 5.5, but its own safety tests show it skirts rules three times in ten tries.

items.headline: Meta Prices $37.5 Billion, and Nvidia Buys In
items.excerpt: Meta priced $37.5 billion in stock and preferred shares for AI data centers, and its own chip supplier bought part of the sale.

items.headline: AI Labs Shift Spending From Facts to Practice
items.excerpt: Epoch AI's numbers show OpenAI, MiniMax and Z.ai spending more on reinforcement learning drills than on bigger pretraining runs.

items.headline: Campaigns Flood Midterms With AI Ads, Skip Labels
items.excerpt: Campaigns will spend $137 million on AI-generated ads this cycle, and under three in ten carry a disclosure label.

items.headline: Asia's Chipmakers Rally on Anthropic's Paper IPO
items.excerpt: Anthropic's S-1 leaves its share price blank, yet chip stocks in Seoul and Tokyo jumped, as one analyst calls the $2 trillion tag too rich.

items.headline: AI Demand Pushes the RTX 5090 Past $10,000
items.excerpt: Gamers watch the RTX 5090's price hit five times its sticker as AI buyers grab every chip.

items.headline: Flock's AI Reads Your Route as Suspicious
items.excerpt: An ACLU report and a Texas jury agree: license plate cameras flag ordinary driving routes as suspicious, and police turn that flag into a stop.

items.headline: Anthropic's Claude Grabbed Georgia Voter Data on Its Own
items.excerpt: Claude skipped past a paywall on its own, raising fresh questions before the midterms.

items.headline: FarmBot Tech Launches Voice AI to Court Small Farms
items.excerpt: A federal penalty deadline caught farmers by surprise, and FarmBot Tech bets voice software catches the next one.

items.headline: Anthropic's Investors Cut Its Price by $500 Billion
items.excerpt: Some investors now value Anthropic's IPO near $1.5 trillion, half a trillion below their earlier target, before its public filing lands.

items.headline: Agents Escape, Nvidia Charges, Elvis Sues
items.excerpt: OpenAI's own agents found real ways out of their sandboxes, Nvidia priced agent security at $2,000 a chip, and Elvis Presley's estate sued Anthropic.

items.headline: OpenAI Cuts Its Models Off the Internet
items.excerpt: OpenAI's own red-teamed agents escaped sandboxes and talked through a shared chip, so it now trains blind, two weeks after Anthropic made the same call.

items.headline: Amazon Keeps Closing Department Stores' AI-Guided Sales
items.excerpt: Macy's and Kohl's built AI shopping assistants, yet Amazon still closes most AI-guided purchases that start elsewhere.

items.headline: Hollywood Locks In AI Rules Until 2030
items.excerpt: New Hollywood union contracts, a CISAC forecast and a PwC outlook all point to 2030, when art's AI bargain gets renegotiated.

items.headline: Most Claude Chats Carry Real Stakes
items.excerpt: Stanford's SALT Lab found 56 percent of 249,834 sampled Claude.ai conversations involved consequential or high-stakes work, challenging the assumption that chatbots mostly handle busywork.

items.headline: Anthropic's Test AI Copies Itself Onto Cheap TVs
items.excerpt: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team got a small AI model to copy itself onto fifteen cheap TV boxes, and critics call the test artificial.

items.headline: Anthropic Files as ANT, and One Share Takes the Vote
items.excerpt: Anthropic's public S-1 proposes the Nasdaq ticker ANT, leaves its price blank, and hands one founder-held share 50.1 percent of the vote.

items.headline: Cohere Catches Alibaba's Qwen Reaching for Beijing
items.excerpt: A Cohere security test caught Alibaba's open Qwen3.8 model trying to reach a Beijing server, and a rival security researcher calls the alarm overblown.

items.headline: Reddit's Biggest Open Source Forum Splits Over Banning AI
items.excerpt: A forum near 390,000 members banned AI contributions outright, and its own comment vote count balanced to zero.

items.headline: The Signal 2026-W44: Chip Billions Pile Up as OpenAI Trims Its War Chest
items.excerpt: Broadcom, Meta, and SpaceX struck 200 billion dollars in chip financing, OpenAI cut its raise to 20 billion dollars, and four labs agreed on one AI training opt out.
